findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Approach's conditional 'a load-bearing conflicts entry stays' fallback with AC line 3's absolute 'no conflicts entry naming eval' — state which governs (e.g. make the AC/test conditional, or note the fallback voids the ticket pending operator decision).
evidence: Approach: 'If a conflicts entry turns out to be load-bearing for a reason unrelated to inspect-ai, that entry stays, the reason is recorded... and the rest still lands.'
AC: '[tool.uv] has no override-dependencies key and no conflicts entry naming eval, verified by the new tomllib test.'
findings.finding: The Approach section hedges that a conflicts entry may be load-bearing and 'stays' if so, but AC line 3 unconditionally asserts no conflicts entry names eval — the two sections prescribe different end-states depending on the resolver outcome.
findings.location: Approach ('If a conflicts entry turns out to be load-bearing...that entry stays') vs Acceptance Criteria line 3 ('no conflicts entry naming eval')
scenarios: The executor finds a conflicts entry is load-bearing, records the reason, keeps it — then the tomllib test asserting no eval conflicts entry fails and the AC is unmet.
findings.suggested_fix: State that both conflicts entries name the eval extra which is being deleted, so removing the extra necessarily removes them; if either proves load-bearing, that is a blocking discovery to escalate rather than a partial-land path, so the absolute AC stands.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
verify command `grep -rn "inspect_ai" src/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable

verify command `grep -rn "inspect.ai\|inspect_ai" pyproject.toml src/ tests/ .github/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
verify command `grep -rn "eval. extra" src/rebar/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the back-out mechanism for the extra removal (e.g. git revert of the pyproject/uv.lock change restores it, since the extra installed only the unused inspect-ai) and note whether a deprecation window is warranted given the extra installed nothing rebar imports.
evidence: Approach documents the break in CHANGELOG.md and docs/release-notes.md with 'what a consumer installing it should do instead'.
No sentence names a revert/back-out path or expand-contract deprecation window for the extra.
findings.finding: Removing the published [eval] extra is an acknowledged consumer-visible break with documented migration guidance, but the plan names no explicit rollback/back-out mechanism as the rubric requires (acknowledgement + migration guidance alone is insufficient per T4).
findings.location: Approach ('Removing a published extra is a deliberate consumer-visible break')
scenarios: A downstream pin like nava-rebar[eval] in a consumer's lockfile breaks on upgrade with no deprecation period.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line: 'Back-out is a straight revert of the pyproject.toml and uv.lock changes; no deprecation window is offered because [eval]'s sole member (inspect-ai) is never imported, so the extra delivered no functional capability to any consumer.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm README.md:229's `nava-rebar[agents,eval,tracing]` union line is in scope and drop `eval` from it so no documented install command names the removed extra.
evidence: README.md:229 `pip  install 'nava-rebar[agents,eval,tracing]'   # the union, if you want it all`
Plan scope: 'README.md — the [eval] bullet under optional capabilities and the pip install nava-rebar[eval] lines.'
README.md:179 (bullet) and :227 (`nava-rebar[eval]`) are clearly covered; :229 is a union form, not the literal `nava-rebar[eval]`
findings.finding: README.md:229 union line `pip install 'nava-rebar[agents,eval,tracing]'` names the removed `eval` extra and will fail to install after removal, but the plan's README scope names only 'the [eval] bullet ... and the pip install nava-rebar[eval] lines' — ambiguous whether the union line is covered.
scenarios: A user copies the union command after the extra is dropped and hits an install error for the nonexistent [eval] extra
findings.suggested_fix: Update line 229 to `pip install 'nava-rebar[agents,tracing]'` and make the README scope bullet explicitly name the union line.

findings.finding: The plan's _llm_eval_commands.py scope covers only the `rebar llm setup` probe (lines 239/283), but the same file has two further live references to the `eval` extra — the `_prompt_eval` docstring (line 22: 'The live model run needs the eval extra + credentials') and the printed user output (line 93: '→ live run needs the eval extra + credentials'). Both name an extra this change deletes, and both misstate the requirement: the live run's real dependency is the `agents` extra per _live_solver (eval.py:572, 'Needs the agents extra (pydantic_ai)').
findings.suggested_fix: In the `_llm_eval_commands.py` scope bullet, add: update the `_prompt_eval` docstring and the printed live-run hint (currently naming the `eval` extra) to name the `agents` extra, matching `_live_solver`'s documented requirement.
